title: Finite positivity survives renormalized limits
status: Lean checked on pinned Mathlib project
novelty: Reusable local interface; no claim of literature priority
statement: Let K_N be real kernels whose every finite Gram form is nonnegative. Let a_N(x) be real factors. If a_N(x)a_N(y)K_N(x,y) converges pointwise to k(x,y), every finite Gram form of k is nonnegative.
proof: For each finite sample x_i and coefficients c_i, the renormalized Gram form is the Gram form of K_N with coefficients c_i a_N(x_i), hence is nonnegative. Finite sums commute with pointwise limits. A limit of nonnegative real numbers is nonnegative.
stress: The conclusion says nothing about the existence of the pointwise limit, the positivity of a particular cutoff theory, Euclidean reflection structure, or a mass gap. If a pairwise renormalization factor does not split as a_N(x)a_N(y), diagonal congruence does not apply.
use: A precise interface between constructive QFT cutoff limits, positive-definite kernels, and covariance limits.

title: Factorized Wilson-loop normalization target
novelty: Candidate specific to the local Wilson-loop program; priority unassessed
statement: For a reflection-compatible finite family of loop observables L_i, find cutoff factors a_N(L_i) such that the renormalized reflected pair kernel is exactly a_N(L_i)a_N(L_j) times a reflection-positive bare kernel, and prove entrywise convergence on every finite family.
proof: If both hypotheses hold, kernel-psd-limit gives positivity of the continuum kernel. The factorization and convergence hypotheses themselves require new RG estimates and are not supplied by this card.
stress: Corner terms, overlapping loops, and cutoff-dependent counterterms may depend jointly on L_i and L_j. A single finite pair whose normalization does not factor invalidates the stated route; positive two-loop bounds alone do not establish reflection positivity.
use: Turns a vague QFT-to-operator bridge into two checkable manuscript obligations.

title: Weighted finite RG recursion
status: Lean checked in prior corpus audit
novelty: Local formal derivation; no claim of literature priority
statement: For nonnegative u and matrix A, positive weights w, row bound Σ_j A_ij w_j ≤ q w_i with q<1, and recursion u_i ≤ Σ_j A_ij u_j+Cw_i, one has u_i ≤ Cw_i/(1−q).
proof: Take M=max_i u_i/w_i. The row bound gives u_i ≤ (qM+C)w_i; at a maximizing i this yields (1−q)M≤C. The empty-index case is vacuous.
stress: The manuscript must establish the row and recursion bounds uniformly in its actual index sets. For q≥1 the division step fails; a one-node system u≤u+C permits unbounded u.
use: Extracts the finite positive-operator consequence of a Wilson-loop RG recurrence.

title: Conditional polynomial hitting grid
status: Lean checked in prior corpus audit
novelty: Local formal interface; the asymptotic PIT consequence remains unformalized
statement: For polynomial f and polynomial generator g, if the pullback f∘g is nonzero and its total degree is less than |S|, some seed in S^t maps to an evaluation point where f is nonzero. The image hitting set has at most |S|^t points.
proof: Multivariate Schwartz–Zippel bounds the zero fraction on the seed grid strictly below one. Evaluation commutes with substitution; image cardinality cannot exceed seed-grid cardinality.
stress: The nonzero pullback is the hard generator-design obligation. The degree inequality is strict: ∏_{a∈S}(X−a) is nonzero and vanishes on S at degree |S|.
use: A formal seam between algebraic circuit lower bounds and black-box PIT.

title: Multiplicity transfer through ξ′
status: Lean checked in prior corpus audit
novelty: New relative to the two local corpora; external priority unassessed
statement: For sufficiently large T and every ε>0, the proportion of zeta zeros of multiplicity at least three in T<Im ρ≤2T is at most ((1/cMT−1)/2+ε), with multiplicity counted in the denominator.
proof: A zero of ζ of order m≥2 becomes a zero of ξ′ of order m−1 in the strip. Retain the low-multiplicity mass in the corpus rank–trace inequality and optimize its coefficients rather than discarding that information in a distinct-zero count.
stress: The cMT constant and asymptotic rank–trace input are dependencies from zeta23. The threshold in T is non-effective; a numerical linear-program optimum is not a formal optimality proof.
use: Connects analytic zero-counting to a finite linear optimization problem.

title: Two samples determine an orbit merger class
status: Lean checked in prior corpus audit
novelty: Local formalization of affine rigidity; literature priority unassessed
statement: For the shortcut Collatz map, fixed k and starting values x,y, equality of k-step iterates at x+2^kq and y+2^kq for every q≥0 is equivalent to equality at q=0 and q=1.
proof: Each k-step iterate on one residue progression is affine in q. Equality at two distinct q values equates both intercept and slope, so the affine expressions coincide everywhere.
stress: One sample is insufficient: at k=10 the iterates of 7 and 8 agree at q=0 while their odd-step slopes differ. This lemma certifies residue families but does not show every integer descends or merges.
use: A small formal certificate for an infinite family of orbit coalescences.

title: Covariance spectrum loses basket prices
statement: Two two-asset one-period martingale laws can have the same single-asset marginals and identical covariance eigenvalues while pricing the payoff (X₁+X₂−1)₊ differently.
proof: Start at (0,0). Law A assigns probability 1/2 each to (1,1) and (−1,−1); law B assigns probability 1/2 each to (1,−1) and (−1,1). Each coordinate is Rademacher and both covariance matrices have eigenvalues {0,2}. The payoff expectations are 1/2 and 0 respectively.
stress: A spectral-only formula for model-free basket prices is impossible even in this finite case. A valid free-probability bridge must retain oriented eigenvectors, coupling information, or a more informative noncommutative law.
use: Tests the proposed martingale-transport/free-probability bridge against its simplest information-loss mode.

title: Lower semicontinuity bounds blowup-set complexity
novelty: Standard topological observation applied as a bridge stress test
statement: If a maximal-lifespan function τ:X→(0,∞] is lower semicontinuous, its finite-lifespan set is Fσ. Thus this set cannot be Π¹₁-complete under continuous reductions from Polish spaces.
proof: The finite-lifespan set equals ⋃_{m≥1}{x:τ(x)≤m}. Every sublevel set is closed by lower semicontinuity, so the union is Fσ and therefore Borel.
stress: The conclusion needs lower semicontinuity of the specific lifespan map and the stated topology. It does not apply automatically to nonunique weak solutions or arbitrary encodings of data.
use: A direct obstruction to an overstrong logic-to-fluid-PDE undecidability claim.

title: Uniform finite-temperature tropical error
novelty: Classical estimate; included as an exact normalization check
statement: For n≥1, β>0 and real a₁,…,aₙ, with m=max_i a_i: m≤β⁻¹log Σ_i exp(βa_i)≤m+(log n)/β.
proof: The largest summand gives exp(βm)≤Σexp(βa_i); every summand is at most exp(βm), so Σexp(βa_i)≤n exp(βm). Apply log and divide by β>0.
stress: No finite uniform bound survives n→∞ at fixed β. The formula needs a nonempty set and positive β; it alone says nothing about KPZ exponents or stochastic polymer limits.
use: Makes the zero-temperature tropicalization error explicit before any stochastic limit is taken.

title: Undirected homology cannot detect directed deadlock
statement: Two directed graphs can have identical underlying undirected simplicial complex and hence identical ordinary homology, while one has a directed cycle with no sink and the other has a terminal sink.
proof: Orient the three edges of K₃ cyclically for the first graph and transitively (1→2, 1→3, 2→3) for the second. Both have the same undirected edges and clique complex. The cyclic orientation has no sink; the transitive orientation has sink 3.
stress: Ordinary homology forgets edge direction. A topology-to-distributed-systems theorem needs a directed invariant or a model-specific protocol complex; undirected Betti numbers alone cannot certify deadlock freedom.
use: A minimal adversarial test for proposed homology-based distributed-algorithm bridges.

title: Strongly polynomial LP needs geometric shortcuts
status: Elementary implication; upstream theorem not independently replayed
novelty: Local synthesis of two November 24 manuscripts; priority unassessed
statement: Assume the new simple rational polytope families have superpolynomial distance between designated vertices when each move may cross a face of dimension at most s(n)=n^{o(1)}. Then no universal polynomial-step algorithm can be required to connect those vertices while staying at feasible vertices and using only such moves.
proof: The distance d_s(u,v) is the minimum number of allowed moves from u to v. Any allowed algorithmic trajectory is one such path, so its step count is at least d_s(u,v). The assumed family makes d_s grow faster than every polynomial in the facet count.
stress: This is conditional on the upstream polytope construction. It does not obstruct the companion strongly polynomial LP algorithm, which can leave the graph or use nonlocal algebraic operations. Edge diameter alone does not force a slow optimizer unless starting and target vertices are specified.
use: Explains the exact separation between a strongly polynomial algebraic LP method and local simplex-style walks.

title: Three-site tensor price has a triangle-slack premium
status: Lean arithmetic proof checked on pinned Mathlib project
novelty: Local consequence of the new upstream price identity; no literature-priority claim
statement: Assume pairwise shared-bit prices equal Euclidean distances and the three-site price equals half the triangle perimeter. If the longest side is c and the other sides are a,b, the three-site price exceeds the largest pair price by exactly (a+b−c)/2. This is positive for a nondegenerate triangle and zero precisely at triangle-equality degeneracy.
proof: With c=max(a,b,c), subtract c from (a+b+c)/2. The result is (a+b−c)/2. The triangle inequality makes it nonnegative, and strict triangle inequality makes it positive. The Lean file proves these real-arithmetic implications.
stress: The three-site price identity is taken from the upstream tensor-geometry scope and is not proved here. Non-Euclidean price functions or collinear points may remove the strict premium; the conclusion is only as strong as the assumed price identity.
use: An exact quantitative test for proposed tensor-network or metric-geometry sharing laws.

title: Unmerged neighbouring Collatz classes have proportion of order 1/√k
status: Lean checked on pinned Mathlib project
novelty: No earlier proof of the order was found. O. J. Said Duran (doi:10.5281/zenodo.23003524, 2026) proved density one first, lists the rate as open, and records 1/√t as an unmeasured heuristic in his public notes. The Lean statements have not yet had an independent human review.
statement: Let T(x)=x/2 for even x and (3x+1)/2 for odd x. Let U_k be the number of residues r mod 2^k for which T^k(r+2^k t)=T^k(r+2^k t+1) fails for some integer t. There are constants 0<c1≤c2 with c1·2^k/√k ≤ U_k ≤ c2·2^k/√k for every k≥1, and c1=1/8 works. The same two-sided bound holds for the pair x, x+m with any m≠0. In Gao's terms: for every N≥4 the number of n<N whose 3n+1 orbit does not meet that of n+1 within log2 n steps is between c1·N/√(log2 N) and c2·N/√(log2 N). Also Lean checked: density one (Gao's 1993 conjecture, first proved by Said Duran), and for every m≥1 a full residue class on which x and x+m merge.
proof: On a residue class the two iterates p,q satisfy q=3^d p+μ. The state (d,μ) moves by one fair coin per step and (0,0) is absorbing; U_k/2^k is the probability of not being absorbed by time k. Lower bound: absorption needs level d≤1, and a simple random walk stays above it for k steps with probability at least 1/√(2k+2). Upper bound: a potential that is superharmonic off a finite set F and grows linearly in d bounds the chance of reaching level √t before F; a second potential bounds the expected time below level L by O(L); a renewal argument over successive visits to F gives B/√t.
stress: Nothing here says any orbit reaches 1: merged classes may still diverge together. The orbits of 3 and 4 never meet (phase mismatch), so no statement for all n is possible. The constant c2 is not effective in any useful sense; simulation puts the proportion near 11/√k for 10^4≤k≤10^8. The contraction used holds for 3x+1 and 3x−1 and fails for 5x+1.
use: Settles the order of the convergence in Gao-type coalescence densities, in Gao's own formulation: 1−d(N) is of order 1/√(log N). After 66 steps only 48.9% of classes have merged (C_66/2^66=0.4886). The same chain gives exact counts C_k for k≤66 by a transfer computation with about 1.59^k states.
source: artifacts/collatz-coalescence/main.tex; Lean 4.33.0-rc2, Mathlib 51e6992; replayed on a second machine on 2026-11-26

title: Neighbour merging tends to probability 1 only for the multiplier 3
status: Lean checked on pinned Mathlib project
novelty: No earlier statement found. Related: Garcia and Tal (Acta Arith. 90, 1999) prove, for generalized maps below the same contraction threshold, that representatives of merging classes have Banach density zero; they do not treat neighbours, rates, or the range beyond the threshold. Literature priority otherwise unassessed.
statement: Let a≥5 be odd and Ta(x)=x/2 for even x, (a·x+1)/2 for odd x. There is ε>0, depending on a, such that for every k at most (1−ε)·2^k residues r mod 2^k satisfy Ta^k(r+2^k t)=Ta^k(r+2^k t+1) for all integers t. Consequently, for odd a≥3, the proportion of merged residue classes tends to 1 if and only if a=3.
proof: The pair state (d,μ) means q=a^d p+μ and moves by one fair coin per step. With w=|μ|/a^d the function φ=min(1,(1+(2/3)^d)(8/w)^(1/4)) is superharmonic at every state and equals 1 at the merged state, so it bounds the merging probability. Along the all-ones coin word the state stays at levels 0 and 1 and |μ| grows by at least one every two steps, so a state with φ≤2/3 is reached. For a=3 the proportion tends to 1 by the density-one theorem.
stress: A statement about residue classes at each k: it does not exclude that one integer in an unmerged class meets its successor later by coincidence. The ε is far from the truth (exact counts and simulation put the merged proportion near 0.8% for a=5 and 10.7% for a=7). The three scalar inequalities behind φ have margins of only 0.001 to 0.005. a=1 is excluded: there 2^k−1 classes merge.
use: Shows the density-one coalescence of neighbours is special to the multiplier 3 and comes from the contraction (log(1/2)+log(3/2))/2<0.
